original_question: For the free group F_2 on two generators, is the cardinal symmetry number MS_r^+(F_2) uncountable for every finite number of colors r?
target_in_paper: Section 8, Problem 8.18: Is ms_r^+(F_2) uncountable for any finite cardinal r?
correct_elements: Your draft has identified the right group (the free group F_2 on two generators), the right invariant (the successor-cardinal symmetry number ms_r^+), and the right quantifier over finitely many colors. This matches the paper's exact open problem in Section 8, Problem 8.18, and it also aligns with the immediately preceding context noting that ms_2^+(F_2) is already known to be uncountable.
missing_details: The paper's notation is ms_r^+(F_2) (lowercase ms), introduced in Section 8 for groups endowed with their family of central symmetries.
The parameter r is stated in the paper as a finite cardinal, not just informally as a finite number of colors.

To make the question stand alone, one should say what 'symmetric' means in this group-theoretic setting: a subset A of F_2 is symmetric if it is invariant under one of the central symmetries of F_2; equivalently, A = cA^{-1}c for some c in F_2.

Because F_2 itself is countable, saying that ms_r^+(F_2) is 'uncountable' does not mean there is an uncountable monochromatic subset of F_2; rather, by the Section 8 definition, it means every r-coloring of F_2 contains an infinite monochromatic symmetric subset.
The paper places the question in the noncommutative setting after recording the known base case ms_2^+(F_2) is uncountable, so that context should be preserved.
refined_question: Let F_2 be the free group on two generators, equipped with its family of central symmetries, and let ms_r^+(F_2) denote the corresponding successor-cardinal symmetry number from Section 8. Is ms_r^+(F_2) uncountable for every finite cardinal r?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for every finite cardinal r, does every r-coloring of F_2 contain an infinite monochromatic subset A \subseteq F_2 such that A is symmetric with respect to some central symmetry of F_2 (equivalently, A = cA^{-1}c for some c \in F_2)?
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper's exact target. In Section 8 the paper introduces the cardinal symmetry numbers ms_r(G) and ms_r^+(G) for groups with central symmetries, and the open problem stated for the free group is precisely Problem 8.18. The sentence immediately before Problem 8.18 records the known r=2 case for F_2, saying that Theorem 8.15 implies ms_2^+(F_2) is uncountable; Problem 8.18 then asks whether the same remains true for every finite cardinal r. The only substantial implicit points missing from the draft are the paper's exact notation, the central-symmetry meaning of 'symmetric subset', and the fact that uncountability of ms_r^+(F_2) is equivalent here to the existence of an infinite monochromatic symmetric subset in every finite coloring, not to an uncountable subset of the countable group F_2.
